title: HIARNG soldier reflects on Hawaii lava flow mission
description: Sgt. Michael Martinez is a Big Island resident serving in the Hawaii Army National Guard with the 227th Brigade Engineer Battalion. He shares his thoughts on what the Hawaii county mission means to him and how HIARNG soldiers are helping to keep the community safe during the lava flow on the Big Island.

transcript.text: I'm from the corner side, the west side of the island.
Right now that side is getting a big hit with the VOG.
And my family is over there, my kids over there, my wife is over there.
And I'm here working, so it feels good to provide the support and
to also think of this whole island because it's affecting this whole island.
What we do is we drive around the community basically supporting HPD and
observing any type of unsafe acts or anything like that.
We also drive around to kind of show the citizens' residents that we're here and
support of them.
It's important that they know that we're here so that way they don't feel alone.
They see us driving around and they see soldiers driving around and they see,
they don't really get that over here, this is a small isolated area.
So when they see that I believe in their heads, they know they're not forgotten or
dismissed or anything like that.
Another reason we're out here is to deter acts of crime, acts of hate, looting.
A lot of the people, the evacuees that left their homes, they left everything.
Everything's there and a lot of people that think, that's all for grabs.
It's not, so we gotta kind of show that that's what we're here for too.
It's very meaningful because this is something that we as guards men,
this is our priority mission and take care of our home.
I guess no words can really describe that.
